glance: Volkswagen's first pay round with IG Metall ended in 90 minutes with no deal, ACEA figures show battery-electric cars took almost 30% of the EU market in October, and Anthropic's shares slipped below their IPO price. The EU's hybrid import quotas start on 1 December, BYD is in talks to buy a French plant, and Daimler Truck is investing in Swedish foundry-tech firm SinterCast.
brief: Good morning. Here is Vertical News for Wednesday the twenty-fifth of November, covering Tuesday. Volkswagen and IG Metall broke off their first pay round in Emden after about ninety minutes, with no deal. Volkswagen wants a two-year pay freeze, the union wants five percent, and strikes are possible from the first of January. New ACEA figures show battery-electric cars took almost thirty percent of the EU market in October, with Chinese brands such as BYD and Leapmotor growing fastest. And Anthropic's shares fell below their eighty-three dollar IPO price, as AI stocks gave back Monday's gains. In other news, the EU's hybrid import quotas start on the first of December and cover ten origins, with China capped at about one hundred and ninety-two thousand cars. BYD is in exclusive talks to buy the Hambach plant in France from Ineos. Uber and Nuro have started driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis in the Bay Area. Daimler Truck is taking a stake in the Swedish foundry technology firm SinterCast, with plans for AI process control. Xpeng presented WorldGPT, one world model for cars, drones and robots. Google DeepMind agents cut the cost of a fusion quantum algorithm almost twelve times, with every step formally verified. The UK's cyber agency warns that AI hacking tools are exploiting old security gaps. A new benchmark shows top AI agents fail more than a third of everyday tasks. Figma's agent is now in FigJam and Slides. Meta put its Muse assistant inside Instagram messages, but not in the EU. And Tidal will remove more than twenty-nine million fully AI-generated songs.

stories.headline: Volkswagen's first pay round with IG Metall ends without a deal after 90 minutes, raising the risk of strikes in January
stories.why: Europe's largest carmaker is heading into a labour conflict that could disrupt production and supplier call-offs across German plants early next year.
body: Volkswagen and IG Metall opened collective bargaining in Emden on Tuesday and broke up after about 90 minutes without agreement. Roughly 4,500 workers rallied outside, some carrying prop coffins. The next round is set for 15 December in Zwickau. The peace obligation runs out on 31 December, so the union could call warning strikes from 1 January.

The gap is wide. IG Metall wants a 5% rise over twelve months. Volkswagen wants a pay freeze for 2027 and 2028, cuts to bonuses, allowances and paid breaks, and a working week tied to plant utilisation instead of the fixed 35 hours. Management says its operating margin will be no more than 1% this year, against 5.9% in 2024, and its 2030 plan adds 12,000 job cuts on top of the 35,000 agreed in 2024. Works council chief Daniela Cavallo called the proposals no basis for talks.
For suppliers and engineering service firms, the practical risk is stop-start production at Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and other sites in the first quarter, and further pressure on development budgets.

stories.headline: Battery-electric cars take 29.8% of the EU market in October, with Chinese brands taking much of the growth
stories.why: Electric drivetrains are close to a third of new EU cars in a single month, which shifts demand for e-motor bearings, power electronics and EV test capacity.
body: New figures from the carmakers' association ACEA show 279,799 battery-electric cars registered in the EU in October, up 61% on a year ago and 29.8% of a market that grew only 2.6% to about 939,000 cars. Petrol and diesel registrations each fell by about 30%. Full hybrids remain the largest group at 34%, and plug-in hybrids took 11%.

From January to October the EU registered 2.2 million battery-electric cars, a 23.4% share, while petrol and diesel together fell to 27.7%. Germany (94,086 BEVs in October) and France (61,958) led the growth. Chinese brands gained fastest: BYD more than doubled to about 31,000 cars, the Chery group nearly tripled and Leapmotor almost quadrupled. Tesla rose 84% to about 10,200.
For European OEMs and suppliers, the numbers confirm that the EV ramp is finally happening, but that a growing share of the volume is going to Chinese-built cars rather than to local platforms.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares fall below the $83 IPO price as AI stocks give back Monday's gains
stories.why: Anthropic's share price has become the market's reading on what public investors will pay for frontier AI, and it affects funding for the AI tools product teams rely on.
body: Anthropic's shares dropped as low as $76 by midday on Tuesday, below the $83 IPO price and nearly 12% down from Monday's close. The stock opened at $111.50 on its Nasdaq debut on 19 November. Trading below the offer price is usually read as a bad sign, because underwriters tend to price an IPO below where they expect it to trade.
The fall came on a weak day for AI stocks in general. Nvidia lost more than 7% by midday, giving back part of the 30%-plus jump it made on Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

Observers see Anthropic as a test case for the sector. A sustained slide could make private investors more cautious on AI start-up valuations and push back other planned AI listings. For teams that build on Claude, nothing changes in the product for now, but the pressure on the company to show revenue growth rises.

stories.headline: EU hybrid import quotas start on 1 December and cover ten origins, with China capped at 191,780 cars
stories.why: Plug-in, full and mild hybrids built outside the EU will face hard volume caps, which changes sourcing and launch plans for importers and European OEMs with plants abroad.
body: The European Commission has adopted a provisional safeguard that sets import quotas for hybrid cars from 1 December 2026 for 200 days, until 18 June 2027. China's allowance is 191,780 cars, derived from the 350,000-a-year cap agreed with Beijing and split into three sub-periods. Japan, South Korea, Türkiye, Mexico, the UK, the US, Morocco and Serbia also get their own quotas, and all other countries share a residual one.

Country quotas are set at 2025 import levels plus about 15%. Imports above a quota are not taxed but refused. The measure covers plug-in, full and mild hybrids. Range-extender EVs are left out and stay classed as battery-electric, so they remain under the existing EV tariffs.

The Commission says hybrid imports have risen sharply since 2023. Definitive measures could follow within nine months, and a permanent China quota growing 6% a year has been discussed. European makers that build hybrids in the UK, Türkiye or Morocco now have to plan within fixed volumes.

stories.headline: BYD enters exclusive talks to buy Ineos Automotive's Hambach plant in France
stories.why: A second European car plant for BYD would bring Chinese EV production and its supplier needs closer to European engineering hubs.
body: BYD says it is in exclusive talks to buy the Hambach plant in north-eastern France from Ineos Automotive. The site was built by Mercedes-Benz for Smart and later sold to Ineos, which has used it for its Grenadier off-roader. The deal is subject to works council consultation, and no price, timetable or model plans have been given.

BYD says it wants to protect local jobs and create work for regional suppliers. The company already has a plant in Hungary, and a French site would add capacity inside the EU at a time when tariffs and the new hybrid quotas make imports from China more expensive or limited.
For European suppliers, a BYD-run Hambach would be a new local customer, but also a sign that Chinese brands plan to compete with EU-built cars on home ground.

stories.headline: Uber and Nuro start driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis in the Bay Area ahead of a 2027 launch
stories.why: A third robotaxi stack is moving to driverless public-road testing, adding to the evidence base for how such systems are validated before launch.
body: Uber and Nuro have begun testing Lucid Gravity robotaxis on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area with no one behind the wheel. Testing in Houston still uses safety operators. The cars carry high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar and radar. Nuro received its California driverless permit in May, more than six months before this step.

Rides for employees come next, with a commercial launch planned for the first quarter of 2027. Uber has raised its investment in Lucid from $300 million to $500 million, has put nearly $500 million into Nuro, and has lifted its purchase commitment to at least 35,000 Gravity vehicles over six years. The joint engineering fleet was about 100 vehicles earlier this year and is growing as Lucid builds production robotaxis in Arizona.
The programme shows a split model: a vehicle maker, an independent autonomy developer and a ride-hailing operator, each owning a part of the validation and safety case.

stories.headline: Daimler Truck takes a minority stake in Swedish foundry-tech firm SinterCast and plans AI process control
stories.why: It ties a Swedish materials specialist to a major truck maker and brings machine learning into how heavy-duty engine blocks are cast.
body: Daimler Truck will take a minority stake in Stockholm-listed SinterCast through new shares and warrants, combined with a licence for its South African foundry Atlantis Foundries. The size and price of the stake were not disclosed, and SinterCast shareholders vote on the deal on 18 December. Atlantis plans to install its first SinterCast System 4000 Plus at the start of 2027.

SinterCast's process control is used for about two-thirds of the world's compacted graphite iron, a strong cast iron used for heavy-duty engine blocks and heads. The partners plan AI-based predictive process control that combines SinterCast's metallurgy models and software with production data from Atlantis.

For engineering teams, this is a practical case of industrial AI where the value comes from closing the loop between material models and real foundry data. SinterCast says the proceeds will fund growth and acquisitions and add recurring licence revenue.

stories.headline: Xpeng's WorldGPT is one world model that predicts and plans for cars, drones, boats and humanoid robots
stories.why: Carmakers are starting to build one foundation model for all their physical products, which affects how driving functions are trained and tested.
body: Chinese carmaker Xpeng has presented WorldGPT, a world model trained on data from six kinds of machine, including cars, boats, drones and humanoid robots. Given camera footage and a short instruction, it generates video of how a scene might play out, plans the actions needed for a task and explains its reasoning in plain language. Xpeng says it took first place on 12 public benchmarks across video generation, visual understanding, robotics and autonomous driving. These results are company-reported.

WorldGPT is a large cloud-based teacher model. Its knowledge is distilled into smaller models that run on each machine, and developers adapt the base model to each product's tasks and hardware. Xpeng argues this cuts the data and cost needed for each new application.

For simulation and validation teams, generated futures from a world model are becoming a source of test scenarios, which raises new questions about how to check that synthetic scenes are physically plausible.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind agent teams cut the cost of a fusion quantum algorithm 11.8 times, with every step checked in Lean
stories.why: It is a clear example of AI agents doing engineering research where each result is formally verified, a pattern that could carry over to simulation codes.
body: Google DeepMind has described how teams of Gemini 4 agents improved well-known quantum algorithms. Independent teams each worked on one problem, every idea had to be proved in the Lean theorem prover before it entered a shared notebook, and the teams met at a virtual conference every four hours to compare ideas. Researchers chose the problems and supervised progress.

The biggest gain was for simulating inertial confinement fusion: estimated computing cost fell 11.8 times and the number of error-corrected qubits dropped from 5,650 to 4,338. A light-sensitive molecule simulation became about 8 times cheaper, a drug-metabolising enzyme simulation improved 2.5 times, and a routine for loading numbers into quantum states sped up 290 times.

DeepMind has open-sourced the Lean library, problem specifications and verified solutions. The method matters beyond quantum computing: it shows how agent output can be made trustworthy by forcing it through formal checks.

stories.headline: UK cyber agency warns AI hacking tools are exploiting years of weak security basics
stories.why: Engineering and product organisations with old internet-facing systems and loose APIs are the easiest targets for automated attackers.
body: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre says it has seen a marked rise in AI-driven attacks in recent months, including several incidents since September where autonomous hacking tools caused intrusions and downtime. The rise follows the free release earlier this year of open-source autonomous penetration-testing tools.

The NCSC stresses that the weaknesses being used are not new. Attackers are finding weak passwords, exposed internet-facing systems and poorly protected API endpoints, much of it the result of years of technical debt, and AI tools now find them in minutes. Its advice is to keep established security controls, which AI does not make obsolete, and to fix long-ignored gaps.

The warning comes days after the European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack on its own systems. For product and engineering teams, it is a push to review developer APIs, test rigs and legacy tools that are reachable from the internet.

stories.headline: ShellBench: top AI agents fail more than a third of everyday tasks, and 15.7% of attempts break a safety rule
stories.why: It gives product teams real numbers on how often agents fail at ordinary tasks, and shows that the harness around the model changes the result.
body: A new benchmark called ShellBench, built with researchers from the OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat and UC Berkeley, tests agents on everyday tasks drawn from more than 10 million anonymised real interactions. Even the best models failed more than a third of the time, and 15.7% of all attempts broke at least one safety requirement.

The failures are telling. Agents ignored a child's school pickup in 79.5% of relevant tasks, recommended duplicate or wrong invoice payments 40.3% of the time and failed to protect a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. GPT-6 Astra scored highest but passed all three repeated runs of a task less than half the time. Meta's Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in one harness and 38.1% in another.
For PMs shipping agent features, the lesson is that consistency and safety checks need their own evaluation, and that model choice is only part of the outcome.

stories.headline: Figma's agent is now generally available in FigJam and Slides on all paid plans
stories.why: The design tool's agent now covers the planning and presentation steps around design work, not just the canvas.
body: Figma has made its agent generally available in FigJam and Figma Slides on all paid plans, with connectors and file attachments supported in both. In FigJam it can pull context from tools such as Hex, Slack and Asana to build and fill boards and diagrams, and it can turn a messy board into an organised spec with a summary and next steps.

In Slides it can start a deck from an attached spec outline and a brand template, split crowded slides, sharpen key messages and draft speaker notes for a given audience. The release follows the agent's arrival in Dev Mode on 19 November, where it can inspect designs, compare versions and give code snippets.
For design teams, the agent now spans workshop, spec, handoff and stakeholder deck in one tool. The open question is how well it keeps decisions consistent as work moves between those stages.

stories.headline: Meta puts its Muse assistant inside Instagram DMs, first in the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore
stories.why: Assistants are moving into the messaging threads where people already share links and plans, which is a pattern for any app with a chat surface.
body: Meta is rolling out its Muse AI assistant inside Instagram direct messages on iOS and Android. Users can chat with Muse in a thread to get context on a post, place or product, catch up on missed conversations, and act on shared posts, for example adding a café to a travel itinerary or finding a deal on shoes. These chats also appear in the main Muse app.

Muse can also sort saved posts and reels into folders and turn a recipe video into a shopping list or travel clips into an itinerary. Meta says nothing is shared or sent without the user's approval, and users can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions. The launch covers the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore. The EU is not included.
For product teams, it is a clear example of an assistant placed inside an existing social flow rather than in a separate app, with approval steps for every action.

stories.headline: Tidal will remove fully AI-generated songs from 9 December, deleting more than 29 million tracks
stories.why: It is one of the toughest platform policies on AI content so far, and a reference point for any product that has to decide how to treat generated material.
body: Music streaming service Tidal will ban songs generated entirely by AI from 9 December and says it will delete more than 29 million tracks by the end of the year. Distributors will be barred from delivering fully AI-made songs, and uploads whose metadata says they are fully AI-generated will be rejected. Tracks made with AI assistance will still be accepted.

Tidal says more than 43% of uploads in the past 90 days were AI-generated and expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day. It counts 27 million fully AI tracks, 6.3% of its catalogue, and says 96% of them have never been streamed. Demonetising them from June was not enough of a deterrent.

Other services differ: Bandcamp bans AI music, Deezer offers detection and a filter, and Spotify and YouTube Music label it. The split shows there is no settled product pattern yet for generated content.

watch.title: SKF Vertevo listing
watch.text: Wednesday 25 November is the last day to trade SKF shares with the right to Vertevo shares. The record date is 27 November and trading starts on Nasdaq Stockholm on 1 December.

watch.title: Polestar results today
watch.text: Polestar publishes select third-quarter and nine-month figures on Wednesday before the market opens, with a call at 14:00 CET.

watch.title: VW talks resume 15 December
watch.text: Volkswagen and IG Metall meet again in Zwickau on 15 December. Without a deal, warning strikes are possible from 1 January.
